newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. to remove single entry bond rules on HK suits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to remove single entry bond rules on HK suits.

text.p: U.S. customs will remove the single entry bonding requirements that it imposed in June on two categories of suits exports from the territory, the Hong Kong government said in a statement on Wednesday.
U.S. customs officials announced the plan in a meeting with their Hong Kong counterparts in Washington on Monday, the statement said.
Since June 17, 10 categories of Hong Kong textiles products covering suits, skirts, nightwear, underwear to dresses have been subject to additional import measures imposed by the U.S. Customs.

They include additional requirements in import documentation, the requirement for a single entry bond, and the requirement for joint verification by Hong Kong and U.S. Customs of the origin of consignments.
Also, since September 1, four more categories covering cotton gloves, cotton knit shirts, women's cotton pants, and cotton dressing gowns have been placed on a "watch list".
The extra requirements were intended to ensure the Hong Kong origin of the goods, following suspicions in the U.S. that some items were illegally transshipped from China.
Hong Kong has objected to unilateral imposition of these requirements, pointing out that they are applied to the relevant products only from Hong Kong and are therefore discriminatory.
But the government statement did not say when the U.S. would remove the single entry bonding requirements on suits.

In the Monday meeting, U.S. Customs officials said the single entry bonding requirements would continue for the remaining eight categories of textile products, and the "watch list" would continued to be monitored.
The U.S. would take appropriate action based on the joint team findings on any goods that transhipping companies shipped or had shipped, the Hong Kong government quoted U.S. officials as saying.
